source_refs.note: Practice MCQs written from Chapter 1 (PDF 4-32, printed 1-29); not printed in the book. Based on the chapter's text, tables, boxes and worked examples (numericals with changed values); none repeats the chapter exercise. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Chapter 1 (Introduction to Software Development), arranged by the chapter's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation; numerical questions show the working.

blocks.prompt: 1 Software development is a systematic process that transforms ______ into software products.
blocks.explanation: Software development is a systematic process that transforms user needs into software products (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: Software development is a systematic process that transforms user needs into software products

blocks.prompt: 2 Understanding the software development process is crucial for creating software solutions that are:
blocks.explanation: The Introduction says that understanding the process is crucial for creating reliable, maintainable and scalable software solutions.

book_ref.quote: Understanding the software development process is crucial for creating reliable, maintainable, and scalable software solutions

blocks.prompt: 3 Software development is the process of:

options.text: assembling the parts of a computer
creating computer programs designed to perform specific tasks

blocks.explanation: Section 1.1: software development is the process of creating computer programs designed to perform specific tasks; it involves writing code, testing it and addressing issues.

book_ref.quote: Software development is the process of creating computer programs designed to perform specific tasks

blocks.prompt: 4 According to the book, which software helps us manage our money?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.1 gives three examples: social media to communicate with friends, banking apps to manage money and educational games to make learning fun.

book_ref.quote: helps us manage our money with banking apps

blocks.text: 1.2 Introduction to Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC)

blocks.prompt: 5 The SDLC defines the processes used to build an application from:

options.text: its initial conception to its deployment and maintenance

blocks.explanation: Section 1.2: SDLC is a framework that defines the processes used to build an application from its initial conception to its deployment and maintenance.

book_ref.quote: defines the processes used by organizations to build an application from its initial conception to its deployment and maintenance

blocks.prompt: 6 Besides meeting customer expectations, the software delivered through SDLC should:

options.text: be completed within time and cost estimates and work efficiently

blocks.explanation: Section 1.2: SDLC aims at high-quality software that meets or exceeds customer expectations, reaches completion within time and cost estimates, and works efficiently.

book_ref.quote: reaches completion within time and cost estimates, and works efficiently

blocks.prompt: 7 In software engineering, a framework is a standardized and reusable set of:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.1: a framework is a standardized and reusable set of concepts, practices and tools that gives a structured foundation for developing applications.

book_ref.quote: a framework is a standardized and reusable set of concepts, practices, and tools

blocks.prompt: 8 Which of the following is NOT a ready-made feature of Django named in the book?

options.text: Translating C programs into machine code

blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.1: Django (a framework for websites) comes with user login, database management and page templates. Translating C into machine code is the work of a compiler such as GCC.

book_ref.quote: Django comes with ready-made features like user login, database management, and page templates

blocks.prompt: 9 Using a framework mainly allows developers to:

options.text: focus on code specific to their application instead of reinventing common solutions

blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.1: a framework offers predefined components, so developers focus on code specific to their application rather than reinventing common solutions; frameworks promote efficiency, consistency and code reusability.

book_ref.quote: Frameworks promote efficiency, consistency, and code reusability

blocks.prompt: 10 Which is the correct order of the SDLC stages described in the book?

options.text: Requirement gathering, Design, Development, Testing, Deployment, Maintenance
Design, Requirement gathering, Testing, Development, Maintenance, Deployment
Development, Design, Requirement gathering, Deployment, Testing, Maintenance
Requirement gathering, Development, Design, Deployment, Testing, Maintenance

blocks.explanation: Sections 1.2.2.1 to 1.2.2.6 take the stages in order: requirement gathering, design, development, testing, deployment and maintenance.

book_ref.quote: It is used by software developers and engineers to guide the design, development, and testing of software

blocks.prompt: 11 In which SDLC phase do developers talk to users and stakeholders to find out their needs and expectations?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.1: in the initial phase, requirement gathering, developers talk to users and other stakeholders to collect what the software needs to achieve.

book_ref.quote: In this initial phase, the goal is to understand and collect what the software needs to achieve

blocks.prompt: 12 Watching how users work with the current system to find problems is the requirement-gathering activity called:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.1: observations means watching how users interact with current systems to identify problems and opportunities for improvement.

book_ref.quote: Watching how users interact with current systems to identify problems and opportunities for improvement

blocks.prompt: 13 Studying existing reports and user manuals to gather more information about requirements is called:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.1: document review is looking at existing documents, such as reports and user manuals, to gather additional information about the requirements.

book_ref.quote: Looking at existing documents, such as reports and user manuals

blocks.prompt: 14 The book compares requirement gathering to:

options.text: planning a big event, like a wedding
drawing a blueprint of a house

blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.1 (Did You Know): just as you need to know the preferences of the bride and groom, developers need to know what users want.

book_ref.quote: Requirement gathering is similar to planning a big event, like a wedding

blocks.prompt: 15 Requirements that outline the tasks, services and functionalities a system must perform are:
blocks.explanation: Functional requirements describe the specific behaviors or functions of a system: what the system should do, including tasks, services and functionalities.

book_ref.quote: Functional requirements describe the specific behaviors or functions of a system

blocks.prompt: 16 'The system should handle up to 1000 simultaneous users without slowing down' is which non-functional requirement?
blocks.explanation: In the library example, handling up to 1000 simultaneous users without performance degradation is the performance requirement.

book_ref.quote: The system should handle up to 1000 simultaneous users without performance degradation

blocks.prompt: 17 A library system 'should be available 99.9% of the time with minimal downtime'. This is a:
blocks.explanation: Reliability (non-functional): the system should be available 99.9% of the time, ensuring high availability and minimal downtime.

book_ref.quote: The system should be available 99.9% of the time

blocks.prompt: 18 Which of the following is a FUNCTIONAL requirement of a library management system?

options.text: Librarians can add, update and remove books from the inventory
The interface should be easy to navigate
The system should scale to more users

blocks.explanation: Inventory management (librarians add, update and remove books) is a function the system performs; encryption, ease of use and scaling are non-functional.

book_ref.quote: Librarians should be able to add, update, and remove books from the inventory

blocks.prompt: 19 Encrypting user data and controlling access through secure authentication is the non-functional requirement of:
blocks.explanation: Security: user data should be encrypted, and access should be controlled through secure authentication mechanisms.

book_ref.quote: access should be controlled through secure authentication mechanisms

blocks.prompt: 20 According to Table 1.1, which statement is true for functional requirements?

options.text: They define the quality attributes and constraints of the system
They describe how the system should perform
They are directly related to user interactions and system tasks
They are related to usability and reliability

blocks.explanation: Table 1.1: functional requirements are directly related to user interactions and system tasks; the other three describe non-functional requirements.

book_ref.quote: Directly related to user interactions and system tasks

blocks.prompt: 21 The design phase of SDLC is compared in the book to:

options.text: following a recipe to bake a cake
drawing a blueprint before building a house

blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.2: in design we plan how the software will look and work; it is like drawing a blueprint before building a house.

book_ref.quote: This is like drawing a blueprint before building a house

blocks.prompt: 22 Creating mockups of the user interface belongs to which design activity?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.2: Develop Models represents the software's structure and could include mockups of the user interface.

book_ref.quote: This could include creating mockups of the user interface

blocks.prompt: 23 Deciding the overall structure of the software and how its components will interact is called:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.2: Plan the Architecture decides the overall structure of the software, including how different components will interact.

book_ref.quote: To decide the overall structure of the software, including how different components will interact

blocks.prompt: 24 In the design phase, a flowchart is drawn to:

options.text: install the software on the user's system
map out the steps the program will take to complete a task
merge code into a central repository

blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.2 (Create Diagrams): for example, we draw a flowchart to map out the steps the program will take to complete a task.

book_ref.quote: we draw a flowchart to map out the steps the program will take to complete a task

blocks.prompt: 25 In the development phase, 'code' means:

options.text: a drawing of the user interface
a set of instructions that the computer follows to perform specific tasks

blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.3: programmers write the code, which is a set of instructions that the computer follows to perform specific tasks.

book_ref.quote: This is where programmers write the code, which is a set of instructions that the computer follows to perform specific tasks

blocks.prompt: 26 In the book's recipe analogy for the development phase, the design specifications are:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.3: the design specifications are the recipe, and coding is the process of mixing and baking the ingredients to make a cake.

book_ref.quote: the design specifications are the recipe, and coding is the process of mixing and baking the ingredients

blocks.prompt: 27 During the development phase, if programmers find issues in their code they:

options.text: revise the code, correct the problems and test again

blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.3: programmers test their code; if issues are found they revise the code, correct the problems and test again until the software is ready for the next stage.

book_ref.quote: If any issues are found, programmers revise the code, correct the problems, and test again

blocks.prompt: 28 The book describes the testing phase of SDLC as a:

options.text: quality check to make sure everything works as expected

blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.4: testing is checking the software to identify bugs, errors or issues; think of it as a quality check.

book_ref.quote: Think of it as a quality check to make sure everything works as expected

blocks.prompt: 29 Checking whether software works well under high traffic or heavy data is:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.4: performance testing checks if the software performs well under different conditions, such as high traffic or heavy data.

book_ref.quote: Checking if the software performs well under different conditions, such as high traffic or heavy data

blocks.prompt: 30 Compatibility testing makes sure that the software:

options.text: has all features according to the specifications
works well on various devices and operating systems

blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.4: compatibility testing makes sure the software works well on various devices and operating systems.

book_ref.quote: Making sure the software works well on various devices and operating systems

blocks.prompt: 31 Making the tested software available for users to access and use is called:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.5: after testing and fixing, the software moves to deployment, the process of making it available for users.

book_ref.quote: Deployment is the process of making the software available for users to access and use

blocks.prompt: 32 Setting up user preferences, network settings and database connections during deployment is:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.5: configuration adjusts the software to the needs of the user or organization, e.g. user preferences, network settings and database connections.

book_ref.quote: This can include setting up user preferences, network settings, and database connections

blocks.prompt: 33 During deployment, running a program that copies files onto the user's system or server is part of:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.5: installation puts the software on the user's system or server, which may involve running an installation program that copies files.

book_ref.quote: running an installation program that copies files and sets up necessary configurations

blocks.prompt: 34 Why is the software tested in its real-world environment after installation?

options.text: To write the first version of the code
To ensure it works correctly with other systems and meets user needs
To collect requirements from the users

blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.5: after installation the software is tested in its real-world environment to ensure it works correctly with other systems and meets user needs.

book_ref.quote: After installation, the software is tested in its real-world environment

blocks.prompt: 35 'You need to water it regularly and address any problems to keep it healthy.' This analogy describes which SDLC phase?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.2.2.6: maintenance is like taking care of a plant; ongoing updates keep the software working and adapted to changes in user needs or technology.

book_ref.quote: Maintenance is like taking care of a plant

blocks.prompt: 36 Structured approaches that guide the planning, creation and management of software projects are called:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3: software development methodologies are structured approaches that guide the planning, creation and management of software projects.

book_ref.quote: Software development methodologies are structured approaches to software development

blocks.prompt: 37 Software process models are:

options.text: lists of bugs found during testing
abstract representations of the processes in the software development lifecycle

blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1: software process models are abstract representations of the processes involved in the lifecycle; they give a framework for planning, structuring and controlling development.

book_ref.quote: Software process models are abstract representations of the processes involved in the software development lifecycle

blocks.prompt: 38 Which importance of process models lets teams predict outcomes and manage risks more effectively?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1: predictability; by following a defined process, teams can predict outcomes and manage risks more effectively.

book_ref.quote: By following a defined process, teams can predict outcomes and manage risks more effectively

blocks.prompt: 39 'Structured methodologies streamline the development process, reducing wasted effort.' This describes:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1 lists predictability, efficiency and quality; efficiency means reducing wasted effort.

book_ref.quote: Structured methodologies streamline the development process, reducing wasted effort

blocks.prompt: 40 In the Waterfall Model, the phases are carried out:

options.text: one after another; each phase is completed before the next begins
in any order the team likes

blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.1: the Waterfall Model is linear and sequential; each phase must be completed before the next one begins, without going back.

book_ref.quote: This model is linear and sequential

blocks.prompt: 41 In the Waterfall Model, the actual code is written in the phase called:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.1: Implementation is the phase in which the actual code is written to create the software.

book_ref.quote: Write the actual code to create the software

blocks.prompt: 42 The Waterfall Model is most suitable for:

options.text: small projects with clear, fixed requirements
projects needing changes after every sprint

blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.1: Waterfall works well for small projects with clear, fixed requirements where changes are unlikely.

book_ref.quote: Works well for projects with clear, fixed requirements where changes are unlikely

blocks.prompt: 43 Which is a limitation (inflexibility) of the Waterfall Model?

options.text: It needs two developers at one workstation
Going back to change a completed phase is difficult and costly

blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.1: inflexibility; once a phase is completed, going back to make changes is difficult and costly.

book_ref.quote: Once a phase is completed, going back to make changes is difficult and costly

blocks.prompt: 44 The 'risk and uncertainty' limitation of the Waterfall Model arises because it assumes that:

options.text: all requirements are known from the start

blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.1: the model assumes all requirements are known from the start, which is risky if new needs or issues arise later.

book_ref.quote: The model assumes that all requirements are known from the start

blocks.prompt: 45 Agile Methodology focuses on:

options.text: completing each phase fully before the next
fixing all requirements at the start
delivering the whole software only once at the end
delivering small, working parts quickly and adapting to changes

blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.2: Agile focuses on delivering small, functional parts of the software quickly and adapting to changes as the project progresses.

book_ref.quote: Agile focuses on delivering small, functional parts of the software quickly and adapting to changes as the project progresses

blocks.prompt: 46 Writing tests before writing the code is the Agile practice called:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.2: Test-Driven Development means writing tests before writing the code to ensure the software works as expected.

book_ref.quote: Writing tests before writing the code to ensure the software works as expected

blocks.prompt: 47 In pair programming:

options.text: two teams test the same software separately
two developers work at one workstation; one writes code and the other reviews it in real time
one developer writes two programs at once

blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.2: in pair programming two developers work together at one workstation, one writing code and the other reviewing it in real time.

book_ref.quote: Two developers work together at one workstation

blocks.prompt: 48 Which Agile practice regularly merges code changes into a central repository?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.2: continuous integration is regularly merging code changes into a central repository to detect and fix issues early.

book_ref.quote: Regularly merging code changes into a central repository to detect and fix issues early

blocks.prompt: 49 Agile improves customer satisfaction mainly because:

options.text: customers never need to give feedback
the full software is delivered only at the end
requirements are frozen at the start
customers see progress through regular delivery of working software and give feedback

blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.2: regular updates and frequent delivery of working software mean that customers can see progress and provide feedback more often.

book_ref.quote: Regular updates and frequent delivery of working software mean that customers can see progress

blocks.prompt: 50 Which of these is a limitation of Agile Methodology?

options.text: It assumes all requirements are known from the start
It needs active participation from all stakeholders
Changes are not allowed after development starts
It has no feedback from customers

blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.2: Agile limitations are scaling challenges, the need for active participation of all stakeholders, and being less predictable.

book_ref.quote: Agile requires active participation from all stakeholders

blocks.prompt: 51 Why is it harder to predict the exact timeline and scope of an Agile project?

options.text: Because only one developer works on it
Because Agile projects evolve through feedback and changes

blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.2 (less predictable): since Agile projects evolve through feedback and changes, the exact timeline and scope are harder to predict.

book_ref.quote: Since Agile projects evolve through feedback and changes

blocks.prompt: 52 Scrum is:

options.text: an agile framework for managing and completing complex software projects

blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.3: Scrum is an agile framework widely used for managing and completing complex software projects.

book_ref.quote: Scrum is an agile framework widely used for managing and completing complex software projects

blocks.prompt: 53 The Scrum framework is built around:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.3: the Scrum framework is built around a set of roles, events and artifacts.

book_ref.quote: The framework is built around a set of roles, events, and artifacts

blocks.prompt: 54 In Scrum, who defines the product backlog and keeps the team on the highest-priority items?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.3: the Product Owner defines the product backlog and ensures the team works on the highest-priority items.

book_ref.quote: The Product Owner defines the product backlog and ensures that the team is working on the highest-priority items

blocks.prompt: 55 Who is responsible for delivering the product increments in Scrum?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.3: the Development Team, consisting of cross-functional members, is responsible for delivering the product increments.

book_ref.quote: The Development Team, consisting of cross-functional members, is responsible for delivering the product increments

blocks.prompt: 56 In Scrum, time-boxed iterations are called:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.3: Scrum events include Sprints (time-boxed iterations), Sprint Planning, Daily Standups, Sprint Reviews and Sprint Retrospectives.

book_ref.quote: These include Sprints (time-boxed iterations)

blocks.prompt: 57 Which of the following is NOT a Scrum event?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.3: the Product Backlog is a Scrum artifact (a prioritized list of features); the others are events.

book_ref.quote: Sprint Planning, Daily Standups, Sprint Reviews, and Sprint Retrospectives

blocks.prompt: 58 In Scrum, the working product that results from the current Sprint is the:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.3: the Increment is the working product that is the result of the current Sprint.

book_ref.quote: Increment (the working product that is the result of the current Sprint)

blocks.prompt: 59 A list of tasks to be completed in one Sprint is the:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.3: the Sprint Backlog is a list of tasks to be completed in a Sprint; the Product Backlog is the prioritized list of all features and requirements.

book_ref.quote: Sprint Backlog (a list of tasks to be completed in a Sprint)

blocks.prompt: 60 Which kind of project does the book name as suitable for Scrum?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.3: Scrum suits mobile applications and web development; embedded systems and safety-critical software (medical, aerospace) are not suitable.

book_ref.quote: Mobile app development often involves continuous feedback and rapid iterations

blocks.prompt: 61 Lean Software Development is derived from:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.3: Lean Software Development is derived from Lean manufacturing principles and focuses on delivering value to the customer.

book_ref.quote: Derived from Lean manufacturing principles

blocks.prompt: 62 The Lean principle that removes activities which add no value to the customer is:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.3: Eliminate Waste means identifying and removing activities that do not add value to the customer.

book_ref.quote: Identify and remove activities that do not add value to the customer

blocks.prompt: 63 'Make decisions based on the latest possible information to reduce uncertainty' is the Lean principle:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.3: Decide as Late as Possible means making decisions on the latest possible information to reduce uncertainty.

book_ref.quote: Make decisions based on the latest possible information to reduce uncertainty

blocks.prompt: 64 Which Lean principle asks the team to consider the entire system and its context?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.3: See the Whole means considering the entire system and its context to optimize the overall flow of work.

book_ref.quote: Consider the entire system and its context to optimize the overall flow of work

blocks.prompt: 65 Giving teams the authority and responsibility to make decisions is the Lean principle:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.3: Empower the Team gives teams the authority and responsibility to make decisions and solve problems.

book_ref.quote: Give teams the authority and responsibility to make decisions and solve problems

blocks.prompt: 66 For which project is Lean Software Development NOT ideal, according to the book?

options.text: Software for an aviation control system

blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.3: Lean is not ideal for complex or regulated projects; an aviation control system demands rigorous documentation, extensive testing and regulatory compliance.

book_ref.quote: developing software for an aviation control system would demand rigorous documentation

blocks.prompt: 67 DevOps combines:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.4: DevOps is a set of practices that combines software development (Dev) and IT operations (Ops).

book_ref.quote: DevOps is a set of practices that combines software development (Dev) and IT operations (Ops)

blocks.prompt: 68 The primary goal of DevOps is to:

options.text: make the lifecycle longer and more documented
keep development and operations teams apart
shorten the development lifecycle, improve quality and provide continuous delivery

blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.4: the primary goal of DevOps is to shorten the development lifecycle, improve software quality and provide continuous delivery with high reliability.

book_ref.quote: The primary goal of DevOps is to shorten the development lifecycle

blocks.prompt: 69 In DevOps, CI/CD stands for:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.4 (faster time-to-market): automating processes and enabling continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) lets teams deliver updates more rapidly.

book_ref.quote: By automating processes and enabling continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD)

blocks.prompt: 70 The book's example of a platform that uses DevOps to continuously release new features is:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.4: DevOps is ideal for web, mobile and cloud services; Amazon's e-commerce platform uses DevOps to continuously release features.

book_ref.quote: Amazon's e-commerce platform uses DevOps to continuously release new features and updates

blocks.prompt: 71 DevOps may be less suitable for:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.3.1.4: DevOps may be less suitable for highly regulated or hardware-dependent projects; medical-device software needs rigorous testing and compliance.

book_ref.quote: software for medical devices needs rigorous testing and compliance

blocks.prompt: 72 The book compares planning a software project to planning a trip because in both you need to know:

options.text: only which programming language to use
where you are going, how long it will take and how much it will cost
only how the software will look

blocks.explanation: Section 1.4: planning a software project is like planning a trip; you need to know where you are going, how long it will take and how much it will cost.

book_ref.quote: Planning a software project is like planning a trip

blocks.prompt: 73 According to the book, as of 2023 Microsoft's market capitalization exceeded:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.4.1 (Did You Know): as of 2023 Microsoft had a market capitalization exceeding $2 trillion, showing the economic importance of software development.

book_ref.quote: Microsoft, one of the leading software giants, has a market capitalization exceeding $2 trillion

blocks.prompt: 74 Deciding how long each part of a project will take is called:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.4.2: setting project timelines means deciding how long each part of the project will take; it keeps the project on track.

book_ref.quote: Setting project timelines means deciding how long each part of the project will take

blocks.prompt: 75 Estimating the cost of a software project involves:

options.text: recording the expenses after the project ends
predicting the total expenses required to complete the project

blocks.explanation: Section 1.4.3: cost estimation involves predicting the total expenses required to complete the project; it helps budgeting and resource allocation.

book_ref.quote: It involves predicting the total expenses required to complete the project successfully

blocks.prompt: 76 In cost estimation, the 'development team' factor depends on:

options.text: the colour of the user interface
the number of users after release
the number of developers, their expertise and their hourly rates

blocks.explanation: Section 1.4.3: the development team cost depends on the number of developers, their expertise and their hourly rates.

book_ref.quote: The cost depends on the number of developers, their expertise, and their hourly rates

blocks.prompt: 77 Why do longer projects generally cost more?

options.text: Resources stay engaged longer and the scope may change

blocks.explanation: Section 1.4.3: longer projects incur higher costs due to prolonged resource engagement and potential changes in scope.

book_ref.quote: Longer projects generally incur higher costs due to prolonged resource engagement

blocks.prompt: 78 In the book's online shopping app example, which technology is used for the database?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.4.3: the app uses React Native for cross-platform compatibility, Node.js for the backend and MongoDB for the database.

book_ref.quote: Node.js for the backend, and MongoDB for the database

blocks.prompt: 79 In the example, 2 backend developers work 30 hours/week for 24 weeks at PKR 4,000/hour. Their cost is:
blocks.explanation: 2 x 4,000 x 30 x 24 = PKR 5,760,000 (Section 1.4.3 cost breakdown).

book_ref.quote: PKR 4,000/hour x 30hours/week x 24weeks = PKR 5,760,000

blocks.prompt: 80 In the cost breakdown, the items add up to PKR 18,040,000. The 10% contingency fund is:
blocks.explanation: 10% of PKR 18,040,000 = PKR 1,804,000 (the book's printed PKR 1,604,000 is a misprint; see the Book correction).

book_ref.quote: The items above add up to PKR 18,040,000

blocks.prompt: 81 What is the correct total estimated cost of the online shopping app in the book's example?
blocks.explanation: PKR 18,040,000 + PKR 1,804,000 = PKR 19,844,000 (the printed PKR 19,644,000 is corrected in the book-correction box).

book_ref.quote: The correct total is PKR 18,040,000 + PKR 1,804,000 = PKR 19,844,000

blocks.prompt: 82 According to the book, a person who does not know programming can start a software project by:

options.text: posting the idea on freelancing platforms where developers bid on it
waiting until he learns all languages

blocks.explanation: Section 1.4.3 (Tidbits): you can post your idea on freelancing platforms where developers bid, and seek investors to fund it.

book_ref.quote: With the help of your family, you can also seek out investors to fund your idea

blocks.prompt: 83 A shortage of resources during a software project is an example of:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.4.4: technical risks (technology changes), operational risks (resource shortages) and external risks (market fluctuations).

book_ref.quote: operational risks, like resource shortages

blocks.prompt: 84 Evaluating how likely each risk is and how much it would affect the project is the step:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.4.4: Analyze Risks evaluates the likelihood and impact of each risk, which helps in prioritizing.

book_ref.quote: Evaluate the likelihood of each risk occurring and its potential impact on the project

blocks.prompt: 85 For a project using a new, untested technology, the book's mitigation strategy is to:

options.text: run a small-scale pilot project to test the technology first
use the technology at once in the main project

blocks.explanation: Section 1.4.4: conduct a small-scale pilot project to test the technology before fully integrating it into the main project.

book_ref.quote: Conduct a small-scale pilot project to test the technology before fully integrating it into the main project

blocks.prompt: 86 The last step of risk assessment and management, which continues throughout the project, is:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.4.4: Monitor and Review continuously watches for new risks and reviews existing ones to adjust strategies.

book_ref.quote: Continuously monitor the project for new risks and review existing risks

blocks.prompt: 87 Which of the following is NOT a quality assurance method named in the book?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.4.5: quality assurance uses testing, reviewing code, getting feedback from stakeholders and regularly checking progress.

book_ref.quote: It involves methods such as testing, reviewing code, getting feedback from stakeholders

blocks.prompt: 88 Graphical representation of software systems means:

options.text: writing the code in a graphics language
printing the source code in colour
using visual diagrams to show a system's structure and behaviour

blocks.explanation: Section 1.5: graphical representation uses visual diagrams to depict a software system's structure and behaviour, e.g. UML diagrams.

book_ref.quote: Graphical representation of software systems involves using visual diagrams

blocks.prompt: 89 UML stands for:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.5.1: Unified Modeling Language (UML) is a standardized way to visualize the design of a software system.

book_ref.quote: Unified Modeling Language (UML) is a standardized way to visualize the design of a software system

blocks.prompt: 90 The 'Three Amigos' who created UML are:

options.text: Erich Gamma, Richard Helm and Ralph Johnson
Winston Royce, Ralph Johnson and John Vlissides
Erich Gamma, Grady Booch and John Vlissides
Grady Booch, James Rumbaugh and Ivar Jacobson

blocks.explanation: Section 1.5.1 (Did You Know): UML was created by Grady Booch, James Rumbaugh and Ivar Jacobson, the 'Three Amigos'. Gamma, Helm, Johnson and Vlissides are the 'Gang of Four' of design patterns.

book_ref.quote: UML was created by three software engineers: Grady Booch, James Rumbaugh, and Ivar Jacobson

blocks.prompt: 91 In a Use Case Diagram, the users who interact with the system are called:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.5.2.1: use case diagrams depict the ways in which users, referred to as actors, interact with a system.

book_ref.quote: used to depict the various ways in which users, referred to as actors, interact with a system

blocks.prompt: 92 In use case modelling, an actor can be:

options.text: a human user or another system
only a method of a class

blocks.explanation: Section 1.5.2.1 (Identify Actors): actors can be human users or other systems.

book_ref.quote: Actors can be human users or other systems

blocks.prompt: 93 Reviewing the identified use cases with stakeholders is the step called:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.5.2.1: the steps are Identify Actors, Define Goals, Outline Interactions and Validate Use Cases (review with stakeholders).

book_ref.quote: Review the identified use cases with stakeholders to ensure they accurately capture the required functionalities

blocks.prompt: 94 In the online shopping platform class activity, which one is an ACTOR?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.5.2.1 (Class Activity): the actors are Customer, Administrator and Delivery Personnel; the others are use cases.

book_ref.quote: There is also a feature for delivery personnel to update the status of deliveries

blocks.prompt: 95 In the book's 'organizing your room' class diagram, a box is like a:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.5.2.2: a box serves as a container within the room, akin to a class in a diagram.

book_ref.quote: Serves as a container within the room, akin to a class in a diagram

blocks.prompt: 96 In the room example, 'open' and 'close' represent the class's:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.5.2.2: boxes can perform actions like 'open' or 'close', similar to methods that define what the box can do.

book_ref.quote: similar to methods in a class diagram that define what the box can do

blocks.prompt: 97 In a UML class diagram, the link from ToyBox to the general Box class (inheritance) is drawn with:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.5.2.2 (Book correction): in UML, inheritance is shown with a hollow triangle arrowhead.

book_ref.quote: in UML inheritance is shown with a hollow triangle arrowhead

blocks.prompt: 98 Which UML diagram shows the flow of messages between objects over time?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.5.2.3: sequence diagrams show how objects interact in a particular sequence and the flow of messages over time.

book_ref.quote: They help in understanding the flow of messages between objects over time

blocks.prompt: 99 In the sequence diagram of the user organizing boxes, the 'put toys/books/clothes inside' arrows go:

options.text: from the User to each box
from each box to the User
from one box to another box
from the User back to the User

blocks.explanation: Section 1.5.2.3 (Book correction): the user puts the items into the boxes, so these arrows go from the User to each box.

book_ref.quote: the user puts the items into the boxes, so these arrows go from the User to each box

blocks.prompt: 100 Which UML diagram is useful for modelling the logic of complex operations as a flow of steps?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.5.2.4: activity diagrams illustrate the flow of activities or steps in a process and model the logic of complex operations.

book_ref.quote: They are useful for modeling the logic of complex operations

blocks.prompt: 101 In the restaurant activity diagram, which activity comes right after 'Order Placement'?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.5.2.4: Start, Order Placement, Food Preparation, Order Delivery, End; arrows show the sequence.

book_ref.quote: then to 'Food Preparation,' and finally to 'Order Delivery.'

blocks.text: 1.5.3 Using UML to Represent Software Systems

blocks.prompt: 102 Using UML diagrams to map out the requirements and design before writing any code is the application called:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.5.3: UML is used in planning (before code), development (understanding structure) and communication (with non-technical stakeholders).

book_ref.quote: Use UML diagrams to map out the system's requirements and design before writing any code

blocks.prompt: 103 UML helps non-technical stakeholders understand how a system works. This application of UML is:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.5.3: communication; UML diagrams help team members, including non-technical stakeholders, understand how the system works.

book_ref.quote: UML diagrams help team members, including non-technical stakeholders, to understand how the system works

blocks.prompt: 104 Design patterns are:

options.text: proven solutions to common problems in software development

blocks.explanation: Section 1.6: design patterns provide proven solutions to common problems and serve as blueprints or templates.

book_ref.quote: providing proven solutions to common problems that arise during software development

blocks.prompt: 105 The authors of 'Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software' are known as:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.6 (Did You Know): Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson and John Vlissides are known as the 'Gang of Four'.

book_ref.quote: Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, and John Vlissides

blocks.prompt: 106 Why are some design patterns more commonly used than others?

options.text: Because of their versatility and effectiveness in solving many problems
Because they work only in one language

blocks.explanation: Section 1.6.1: some patterns are more commonly used due to their versatility and effectiveness in solving a wide range of problems.

book_ref.quote: some are more commonly used due to their versatility and effectiveness

blocks.prompt: 107 Which design pattern makes sure that an object is created only once in a program and reused?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.6.1.1: the Singleton pattern makes sure a specific object or resource is created only once and reused whenever needed.

book_ref.quote: a way to make sure that a specific object or resource is created only once in a program

blocks.prompt: 108 The book explains the Singleton pattern with the example of:

options.text: one key to a special room that everyone shares
people getting updates from a source

blocks.explanation: Section 1.6.1.1: it is like one key to a special room; no new keys are made and everyone shares that one key.

book_ref.quote: No new keys are made, and everyone shares that one key

blocks.prompt: 109 In which design pattern do you just ask for what you need and receive the finished product without knowing how it is made?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.6.1.2: the Factory pattern is like a workshop; you tell the factory what you need and it gives you the finished product.

book_ref.quote: you just tell the factory what you need, and it gives you the finished product

blocks.prompt: 110 In which design pattern does a source automatically notify all interested parties when something important happens?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.6.1.3: in the Observer pattern the source automatically notifies all the interested people whenever something important happens.

book_ref.quote: Whenever something important happens, the source automatically notifies all the interested people

blocks.prompt: 111 The main benefit of the Observer pattern is that it:

options.text: keeps things in sync without everyone constantly checking for updates
lets you swap one method for another

blocks.explanation: Section 1.6.1.3: Observer keeps things in sync without everyone constantly checking for updates.

book_ref.quote: It's a way to keep things in sync without everyone constantly checking for updates

blocks.prompt: 112 Which design pattern is like a toolbox from which you pick the right tool for the task and can switch easily?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.6.1.4: the Strategy pattern gives multiple ways to solve a problem; you can switch between them easily without changing much else.

book_ref.quote: like having a toolbox full of different tools, each designed for a specific job

blocks.text: 1.6.2 Applications of Design Patterns in Software Design

blocks.prompt: 113 Design patterns improve communication among developers by:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.6.2: design patterns reduce code complexity, enhance reusability and improve communication by providing a common vocabulary.

book_ref.quote: Improving communication among developers by providing a common vocabulary

blocks.prompt: 114 MVC, a pattern used in web development frameworks like Ruby on Rails, stands for:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.6.2 (Did You Know): the Model-View-Controller (MVC) pattern is used in web development frameworks.

book_ref.quote: the Model-View-Controller (MVC) pattern is used in web development frameworks

blocks.prompt: 115 Software debugging and testing mainly ensure the software's:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.7: debugging and testing are critical stages that ensure the quality and reliability of a software product.

book_ref.quote: Software debugging and testing are critical stages in the software development process

blocks.prompt: 116 In software, a 'bug' is:

options.text: an error or mistake that makes the software behave unexpectedly
a new feature added by users

blocks.explanation: Section 1.7.1: bugs are errors or mistakes in the software that cause it to behave unexpectedly; debugging is finding and fixing them.

book_ref.quote: Bugs are errors or mistakes in the software that cause it to behave unexpectedly

blocks.prompt: 117 Displaying the values of variables at different points of a program to find a bug is the technique of:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.7.1: print statements are added in the code to display the values of variables at different points in the program.

book_ref.quote: Adding print statements in the code to display the values of variables at different points in the program

blocks.prompt: 118 Which debugging practice asks other developers to look at your code to spot errors?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.7.1: code reviews mean having other developers review your code to spot potential errors.

book_ref.quote: Having other developers review your code to spot potential errors

blocks.prompt: 119 Which is the correct order of the testing hierarchy?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.7.2: testing begins with smaller components and progresses to the entire system and user acceptance: unit, integration, system, acceptance.

book_ref.quote: The testing process typically follows a hierarchy that begins with smaller components

blocks.prompt: 120 Testing a single function or method of the software in isolation is:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.7.2.1: unit testing is the first level, where individual components (such as a function or method) are tested in isolation.

book_ref.quote: Unit Testing is the first level of testing, where individual components or modules of the software are tested in isolation

blocks.prompt: 121 Interface errors and data flow between modules are checked in:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.7.2.2: integration testing checks interface errors, data flow between modules and other integration issues.

book_ref.quote: This type of testing checks for interface errors, data flow between modules, and other integration-related issues

blocks.prompt: 122 Testing the complete software as a whole in an environment close to the production environment is:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.7.2.3: system testing tests the entire software as a whole in an environment that closely resembles the production environment.

book_ref.quote: System testing involves testing the software in an environment that closely resembles the production environment

blocks.prompt: 123 The final level of testing, often performed by end-users or clients, is:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.7.2.4: acceptance testing is the final level, often performed by the end-users or clients, to decide if the software is ready for release.

book_ref.quote: It is often performed by the end-users or clients to ensure that the software meets their expectations

blocks.prompt: 124 UAT stands for:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.7.2.4 (Did You Know): acceptance testing is sometimes called User Acceptance Testing (UAT) because it is often done by end-users.

book_ref.quote: Acceptance testing is sometimes called User Acceptance Testing (UAT)

blocks.prompt: 125 Software development tools are used to:

options.text: write, edit, test, debug and manage code

blocks.explanation: Section 1.8.1: software development tools assist in the stages of software creation; they are used to write, edit, test, debug and manage code.

book_ref.quote: Software development tools are programs or applications that assist in various stages of software creation

blocks.prompt: 126 Notepad++, Sublime Text and VS Code are examples of:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.8.2: language editors, also known as code editors, help developers write and edit code; examples are Notepad++, Sublime Text and VS Code.

book_ref.quote: Language editors, also known as code editors, are tools that help developers write and edit code

blocks.prompt: 127 Which code editor does the book describe as 'known for its speed and ease of use'?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.8.2: Notepad++ is simple yet powerful, Sublime Text is known for its speed and ease of use, VS Code has many extensions.

book_ref.quote: Sublime Text: Known for its speed and ease of use

blocks.prompt: 128 A translator that translates code line by line is:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.8.3: interpreters translate code line-by-line (e.g. Python interpreter); compilers translate the entire code at once.

book_ref.quote: Interpreters: Translate code line-by-line (e.g., Python interpreter)

blocks.prompt: 129 Translators convert high-level languages like Python into:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.8.3: translators convert high-level programming languages into machine language (binary code) that computers can execute.

book_ref.quote: Translators convert high-level programming languages (like Python) into machine language (binary code)

blocks.prompt: 130 Which of the following is a compiler for Java programs?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.8.4: GCC (GNU Compiler Collection) for C and C++ and Javac for Java are compilers.

book_ref.quote: Javac: Compiler for Java programs

blocks.prompt: 131 A compiler converts:

options.text: one line at a time during execution
the entire program into machine code before execution

blocks.explanation: Section 1.8.4: compilers convert entire programs from high-level languages into machine code before execution.

book_ref.quote: converts entire programs from high-level languages into machine code before execution

blocks.prompt: 132 GDB is a:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.8.5: GDB is the GNU Debugger for C/C++; Visual Studio Debugger is integrated with Visual Studio IDE.

book_ref.quote: GDB: GNU Debugger for C/C++

blocks.prompt: 133 An IDE brings together:

options.text: editors, compilers, debuggers and version control systems
only a keyboard and a mouse

blocks.explanation: Section 1.8.6: an IDE integrates editors, compilers, debuggers and version control systems in one unified interface.

book_ref.quote: IDE integrate various development tools like editors, compilers, debuggers, and version control systems

blocks.prompt: 134 Which IDE is preferred for Python development?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.8.6: Eclipse is widely used for Java, Visual Studio for .NET and C++, and PyCharm for Python.

book_ref.quote: PyCharm: Preferred for Python development

blocks.prompt: 135 Repl.it and Gitpod are examples of:
blocks.explanation: Section 1.8.7: online platforms are cloud-based and accessible via the internet (e.g. Repl.it, Gitpod); offline platforms are local installations.

book_ref.quote: Cloud-based platforms accessible via the internet (e.g., Repl.it, Gitpod)

blocks.prompt: 136 Source code repositories mainly help in:

options.text: version control, so many developers can work on one project without conflicts

blocks.explanation: Section 1.8.8: repositories store code, track changes, keep a history and help in version control.

book_ref.quote: Repositories help in version control, allowing multiple developers to work on the same project without conflicts

blocks.prompt: 137 Which platform does the book describe as used for both private and public repositories?
blocks.explanation: Section 1.8.8: GitHub is popular for open-source projects; Bitbucket is used for both private and public repositories.

book_ref.quote: Bitbucket: Used for both private and public repositories
